commands.name: describeScreen
commands.description: Read what is on screen right now: which scene is showing, the exact numbers and labels the user can see, and which scenes are reachable. Call this whenever the user asks what they are looking at, and before quoting any number you have not just received from another tool. Never guess a number.

commands.name: askStudent
commands.description: Answer a question about the USER'S OWN degree plan: am I cooked, my risk, a what-if (work hours, course load), which course to take, prerequisites, a stress test, how to get un-cooked. Needs a loaded student (an uploaded audit or a sample student; if none is loaded the result says so). Pass the user's full question in their own words. The app computes the answer from the trained model, moves the screen to the matching scene and returns provenance-checked text in `say`.

question.description: The user's full question about their own plan, in their words, e.g. 'am I cooked' or 'what if I take 3 more credits a term'.

commands.name: exploreCohort
commands.description: Answer a question about PATTERNS across the synthetic cohort, not about the user personally: majors, work hours, course load, internships, first destinations, degree cost by year. Pass the full question. The app queries the database, moves the screen to the resulting chart and returns provenance-checked text in `say` with sample sizes.

question.description: The user's full question about cohort patterns, in their words.

commands.name: showScene
commands.description: Move the screen to one scene. Use for 'show me...', 'go to...', 'open...'. risk = the risk gauge and verdict; timeline = projected time to degree; twins = alumni with a similar profile; drill = the stress test of realistic shocks; repair = the smallest change that gets the user un-cooked; careers = first destination and salary outlook (exploratory, not a promise); models = the Model Lab comparing the four models; explore = the cohort explorer.

commands.name: nextScene
commands.description: Advance to the next scene. Use for 'next', 'continue', 'go on', 'what else'.

commands.name: previousScene
commands.description: Go back to the previous scene. Use for 'back', 'previous', 'go back'.

commands.name: setScenario
commands.description: Change one input of the scenario the user is exploring (the Model Lab controls, or the what-if on their own plan) and re-run the models. Use for 'set internships to three', 'what if I work 30 hours', 'make it a transfer student'. Numbers outside the allowed range are clamped and the result says so. Numeric fields: work_hours 0-50, completed_terms 0-6, credits_per_term 3-18, earned_ratio 0.5-1 (a fraction of attempted credits earned, 0.9 for ninety percent), withdrawals 0-10, failures 0-10, enrollment_gaps 0-4, internship_count 0-4, credential_count 0-8, engagement_count 0-20. Option fields: major (Computer Science or Information Systems), entry_type (First-Time Freshman or Transfer), residency (In-State or Out-of-State).

value.description: The new value as text: digits for numeric fields (for example 30, or 0.9 for earned_ratio), or the option name for major, entry_type and residency.

commands.name: runStressTest
commands.description: Run the fire drill: apply a sequence of realistic shocks to the plan and show how many it takes to get cooked. Use for 'run a stress test', 'fire drill', 'what could go wrong'. Returns provenance-checked text in `say`.

commands.name: findRepair
commands.description: Find the smallest change to the plan that gets the user un-cooked, backed by alumni evidence. Use for 'how do I get un-cooked', 'fix my plan', 'what should I change'. Returns provenance-checked text in `say`.

commands.name: loadSampleStudent
commands.description: Load a synthetic sample student so there is a plan to show. Use for 'load a sample student', 'use a demo student', or when a personal question needs a student and none is loaded. Optional `which`: working (works 22 hours a week, the alarm fires early), cooked (light course load and a heavy job, already cooked), on_track (full loads, on track). Default working.

which.description: Which synthetic sample student to load. Optional.
